# p0_mongodb_atlas_ai (Resource)

A MongoDB Atlas installation for agentic access.

Installing it allows P0 to grant machines just-in-time access to an Atlas project through the Atlas-hosted MCP server, with a token for an MCP configuration that holds only the requested project roles.

**Important:** Before creating this resource you must stage the installation with `p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged` and deploy the connector (its Lambda function on AWS, or its Cloud Run service on Google Cloud). Creating this resource verifies that the connector is deployed. After you create it, add the Atlas service account's client secret as a version of the connector's client secret secret; the connector cannot manage MCP configurations until that version exists.

**Note:** This integration is currently in beta.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Installs MongoDB Atlas for agentic access, with P0's MongoDB Atlas connector on Cloud
# Run and the Atlas service account's client secret in Google Secret Manager.
# Full chain: p0_gcp -> p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged -> Cloud Run connector and client
# secret's secret -> client secret version (added outside Terraform) ->
# p0_mongodb_atlas_ai.

resource "p0_gcp" "example" {
  organization_id = "123456789012"
}

locals {
  project      = "my-project-id"
  project_item = "my-atlas-project"
  # P0 reads the client secret from the secret with this exact ID.
  client_secret_secret_id = "p0_install_mongodb-atlas_${local.project_item}_client-secret"
}

resource "p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged" "example" {
  id               = local.project_item
  atlas_project_id = "0123456789abcdef01234567"

  secret_manager = {
    type       = "gcp-sm"
    project_id = local.project
  }

  depends_on = [p0_gcp.example]
}

resource "google_project_service" "enable_services" {
  for_each = toset([
    "cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com",
    "iam.googleapis.com",
    "run.googleapis.com",
    "secretmanager.googleapis.com",
  ])
  project            = local.project
  service            = each.key
  disable_on_destroy = false
}

resource "google_service_account" "connector" {
  project      = local.project
  account_id   = split("@", p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.connector_service_account)[0]
  display_name = "P0 Cloud Run MongoDB Atlas connector"

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service" "connector" {
  project             = local.project
  name                = p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.connector_service_name
  location            = p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.connector_region
  deletion_protection = false
  # P0 calls the connector from outside GCP; IAM, not origin, gates access.
  ingress = "INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL"

  template {
    service_account = google_service_account.connector.email

    containers {
      image = "docker.io/p0security/p0-connector-mongodb-atlas-ai-gcloud:sha-fced489@sha256:53d208e62c4e3419902f3488fbb651f2f70435d1d9705093c7c2345b56d7477d"

      # The connector also checks this against the caller's OIDC token.
      env {
        name  = "INVOKER_SA_EMAIL"
        value = p0_gcp.example.service_account_email
      }
    }
  }

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member" "invoke_connector" {
  project  = local.project
  location = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.location
  name     = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.name
  role     = "roles/run.invoker"
  member   = "serviceAccount:${p0_gcp.example.service_account_email}"
}

# P0 reads the service to get its invocation URL while it installs. The invoker
# role gives run.routes.invoke only, so it cannot do this read.
resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member" "read_connector" {
  project  = local.project
  location = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.location
  name     = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.name
  role     = "roles/run.viewer"
  member   = "serviceAccount:${p0_gcp.example.service_account_email}"
}

data "google_project" "this" {
  project_id = local.project
}

# The connector keeps each access token in its own secret. GCP checks
# secretmanager.secrets.create on the project, so this binding has no condition.
resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "connector_secret_create" {
  project     = local.project
  role_id     = "p0MongodbAtlasConnectorSecretCreate"
  title       = "P0 MongoDB Atlas connector secret creation"
  permissions = ["secretmanager.secrets.create"]

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_project_iam_member" "connector_secret_create" {
  project = local.project
  role    = google_project_iam_custom_role.connector_secret_create.name
  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "connector_secret_manage" {
  project = local.project
  role_id = "p0MongodbAtlasConnectorSecretManage"
  title   = "P0 MongoDB Atlas connector access token management"
  permissions = [
    "secretmanager.secrets.delete",
    "secretmanager.secrets.get",
    "secretmanager.versions.add",
  ]

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_project_iam_member" "connector_secret_manage" {
  project = local.project
  role    = google_project_iam_custom_role.connector_secret_manage.name
  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"

  # P0 names the access token secrets with this prefix. IAM conditions use the
  # project number, not the project ID.
  condition {
    title      = "P0 MongoDB Atlas access token secrets"
    expression = "resource.name.startsWith('projects/${data.google_project.this.number}/secrets/p0_access-token_mongodb-atlas_${local.project_item}_')"
  }
}

# After apply, add the Atlas service account's client secret as a version of this
# secret. The connector cannot manage MCP configurations until that version exists:
#
#   printf '%s' "$ATLAS_CLIENT_SECRET" \
#     | gcloud secrets versions add p0_install_mongodb-atlas_my-atlas-project_client-secret \
#       --project=my-project-id --data-file=-
resource "google_secret_manager_secret" "client_secret" {
  project   = local.project
  secret_id = local.client_secret_secret_id

  replication {
    auto {}
  }

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member" "client_secret" {
  project   = local.project
  secret_id = google_secret_manager_secret.client_secret.secret_id
  role      = "roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
  member    = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

# The accessor role gives secretmanager.versions.access only. The connector also
# reads the secret itself, and the management role above covers the access token
# secrets alone, so the client secret needs its own grant.
resource "google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member" "client_secret_read" {
  project   = local.project
  secret_id = google_secret_manager_secret.client_secret.secret_id
  role      = "roles/secretmanager.viewer"
  member    = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

# Completes the install; creating it verifies that the connector is deployed.
resource "p0_mongodb_atlas_ai" "example" {
  id               = p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged.example.id
  atlas_project_id = p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged.example.atlas_project_id
  # The client ID of the Atlas service account that P0 manages MCP
  # configurations with. It needs the Project Owner role in the project.
  client_id = "mdb_sa_id_0123456789abcdef01234567"

  secret_manager = {
    type       = p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.type
    project_id = p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.project_id
  }

  depends_on = [
    google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.invoke_connector,
    google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.read_connector,
    google_project_iam_member.connector_secret_create,
    google_project_iam_member.connector_secret_manage,
    google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member.client_secret,
    google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member.client_secret_read,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `atlas_project_id` (String) The 24-character ID of the Atlas project, from Project Settings in Atlas. Must match the `p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged` resource.
- `client_id` (String) The client ID of the Atlas service account that P0 manages MCP configurations with. It needs the Project Owner role in the project.
- `id` (String) The `id` of the `p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged` resource being finalized
- `secret_manager` (Attributes) Where P0's MongoDB Atlas connector runs and stores the Atlas service account's client secret (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--secret_manager))

### Read-Only

- `state` (String) This item's install progress in the P0 application:
	- 'stage': The item has been staged for installation
	- 'configure': The item is available to be added to P0, and may be configured
	- 'installed': The item is fully installed

<a id="nestedatt--secret_manager"></a>
### Nested Schema for `secret_manager`

Required:

- `type` (String) The secret manager that stores the Atlas service account's client secret: `aws-sm` (AWS Secrets Manager, with the connector on AWS Lambda) or `gcp-sm` (Google Secret Manager, with the connector on Google Cloud Run). Must match the `p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged` resource.

Optional:

- `account_id` (String) The AWS account that hosts the connector's Lambda function and the secret that holds the Atlas service account's client secret: one of your AWS Secrets Manager installations in P0. Required for, and only valid with, `aws-sm`. Must match the `p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged` resource.
- `project_id` (String) The GCP project that hosts the connector's Cloud Run service and the secret that holds the Atlas service account's client secret. Required for, and only valid with, `gcp-sm`. Must match the `p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged` resource.
- `secrets_region` (String) The AWS region that stores the secrets, such as `us-west-2`. Required for, and only valid with, `aws-sm`. Must match the `p0_mongodb_atlas_ai_staged` resource.

Read-Only:

- `connector_region` (String) The region in which to deploy the connector: its Lambda function's on AWS, its Cloud Run service's on Google Cloud
- `connector_service_account` (String) The email of the GCP service account that the connector must run as. Google Cloud only.
- `connector_service_name` (String) The name to give the connector's Cloud Run service. Google Cloud only.
- `connector_service_uri` (String) The invocation URL of the connector's Cloud Run service, resolved by P0 during install. Google Cloud only.
